units_signs.current: A (signed in CSV; physical current is |I|, unipolar 0-1.6 A)
units_signs.current_polarity: Train+validation SH: 194 files, 82 negative-mean, 92 positive-mean, 20 near-zero (0 A files); |mean current| matches filename nominal within 0.05 A for ALL 194 SH files. Polarity is a sensor/wiring artifact, not physics; runner sample() uses |I| (legacy v14 _current_pair also used |I|).
units_signs.current_range: 56 train+validation files exceed |I|=1.63 A, max 2.011 A, spikes clustered at step edges (zero-phase filter overshoot on 0->1.6 A steps). Runner tolerance raised 1.63->2.10 A; sample() clamps |I|/1.6 to [0,1].

phase_work_grid_train_validation_SH.method: Fundamental least-squares phase (F vs v) and cycle work W=sum(F*v*dt) on full files, train+validation SH only (n=59 @1.66 Hz, 25 @4.97 Hz, 24 @6.62 Hz). Final test excluded.
phase_work_grid_train_validation_SH.F42_I40_and_F42_I44: Identical F-v phase/work to F42_I42 (force shift same); only F-I relative timing differs, which SH phase cannot select.
phase_work_grid_train_validation_SH.selection_rationale: (42,42) kept as pre-declared centre. (44,44) median lag is closer to zero but goes negative at 4.97/6.62 Hz (F ahead of v, unphysical for a causal damper, suggesting over-shift); (40,40) leaves larger positive residual. Work magnitudes across (40,40)/(42,42)/(44,44) differ by <1%, so work does not select among them. Residual lag after (42,42) is small, positive, and frequency-dependent (not a pure delay), consistent with the MTS qualitative pattern (few ms). 42 ms remains a working hypothesis verified by these gates, not a proven hardware cause.

st_tau_recheck_train_only.method: Event-triggered average, up/down separated (down flipped), steady-velocity windows only (no reversal, |v|>=20 mm/s), fit F = a + b*EMA_delay(|I|) on [-20,+150] ms. Input is zero-phase-filtered recorded current, same as training data, so tau is the effective lag as seen by the model.

results_F42_I42.note: Up/down asymmetry is real (rise slower than fall, or edge-definition difference); a single delay+lag cannot fit both exactly. v19 CurrentLag has no pure-delay term and tau is TRAINABLE in Stage 1, so init is not critical. Init 11 ms kept (pre-declared, within measured range, between the EMA-after-delay values 3-7 ms and the pure-EMA equivalent 15 ms). Old v18 default 20 ms rejected; old v10 implementation was not a true EMA (Codex proof) and is not used as evidence. Learned tau from the Stage-1 best checkpoint must be reported.

st_tau_recheck_train_only.relative_shift_sensitivity: ALL-fit delay: (42,40)=6 ms, (42,42)=8 ms, (42,44)=9 ms. Shifting I by 2 ms moves fitted delay by ~1-1.5 ms (remainder absorbed by tau trade-off). ST fit alone cannot select relative shift; (42,42) rests on the equal-42 ms vs x evidence for both channels and the earlier 0-3 ms residual finding.

normalization_train_only.note: x_ref/x_scale match v17/v18 checkpoint norm (279.1375/63.9665) within 0.004. f_scale differs from v17/v18 checkpoint f_scale 5728.56 because v19 train split includes SH_30mm_4.97Hz_0A (max |F|=7664 N) and re-zeroing; pooled NRMSE is scale-invariant within a run but cross-run pooled values are NOT directly comparable (different validation sets). The valid comparison is v17-control on this aligned validation set, to be run before Stage-1 claims.

short_files_edge_guard.note: Short files are systematic ~2-cycle bursts (SH r2 ~1200 samples, 4.71/4.97 Hz ~400 samples, 6.62 Hz r2 ~295 samples, ST 782-1568 samples), not truncation errors. Runner edge guard: 1000 samples if len>2000, else min(100, len//4). Long files keep the planned 1000-sample guard exactly; short files keep >=50% valid samples. Skipping short files was rejected because it would gut final_test (6/10 short, all 1.6 A files). Rollout burn-in (1000 ms) exceeds short-file lengths, so short-file rollouts are teacher-forced by construction and must be flagged as such at rollout time, not presented as self-rollout evidence.

tau_rationale: Init tau_ms=11.0 kept. ST recheck (train only, aligned data, |I|): up d~15 ms/tau~5 ms, down d~5 ms/tau~3 ms, averaged d~8 ms/tau~7 ms, pure-EMA equivalent tau~15 ms. 11 ms lies within this range and is trainable in Stage 1; the learned tau from the Stage-1 best checkpoint is the real check, not the init value. Old 20 ms default and old v10 non-EMA implementation are not used as evidence.
